items.title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
items.summary: QCon AI New York has published its full program for December 15–16, 2026. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, Pinterest, Honeycomb, Harvey, Google DeepMind and OpenAI describe AI systems they run in production. Talks cover agent permissions and guardrails, eval loops, inference cost, AI code review, and team adoption. By Artenisa Chatziou
items.zh: LinkedIn、Netflix、DoorDash等将分享生产环境Agent、评测与推理成本实践
items.why: 一线生产经验，覆盖权限、评测与成本

items.title: Browse tools.simonwillison.net by tag
items.summary:
Browse tools.simonwillison.net by tag 
I've been wanting a better way to browse my collection of vibe-coded tools (244 and counting) for a while. I had a few Fable 5.2 credits left over before my weekly reset so I set it to work using tree-sitter to analyze the code for JavaScript APIs, libraries, and web API hosts used by each tool. 
 The homepage now features tag clouds for browsing by each of those categories of tag: 
 

 Tags: javascript , tools , ai , generative-ai , llms , claude , vibe-coding
items.zh: 用tree-sitter分析244个工具所用JS API与库，生成标签云便于检索

items.title: JioHotstar Benchmarks Knowledge Bases for AI Coding Agents
items.summary: JioHotstar evaluated 6 approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents using SWE, CodeScale Bench, and an internal question-answering harness. Structural search performed well on concrete tasks, while semantic retrieval helped with ambiguous requirements. The findings highlight trade-offs in accuracy, token use, and tool design, underscoring the need to match retrieval tools to task types. By Leela Kumili
items.zh: 用SWE、CodeScale Bench及内部问答测试6种检索方式，结构检索与语义检索各有优劣
items.why: 为编码Agent选检索工具提供实测依据

items.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
items.summary: United says it won't let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns. The company says it hasn't yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports, in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash.
